instructions: PdfCraft edits PDFs. Open a file with doc_open to get a document id, then inspect (doc_info, text_extract, text_find, page_render) or edit it (page_*, doc_set_info). Edits are undoable (edit_undo) and stay in memory until doc_save. Page numbers are 1-based. Open documents are also resources: pdfcraft://doc/{doc}/info, /text, /page/{page}/text and /page/{page}/image. command_list discovers command ids and tool schemas; command_run executes one, command_batch runs several. doc_inspect returns open document state; render_preview returns a bounded PNG.

tools.name: accessibility_autotag_apply
tools.description: Write marked content, a Document structure element, paragraph tags and a parent tree for every text object in an untagged, text-only PDF. Refuses graphics, images, annotations, forms, existing tags and malformed streams before changing anything. Review all resulting roles; this does not certify accessibility. Undoable.

tools.name: accessibility_autotag_preview
tools.description: Propose paragraph and heading tags for visible text blocks on one page. Returns page bounds, tentative roles and reasons. Does not change the PDF or claim accessibility compliance. Images, tables, lists, annotations and existing structure require separate review.

tools.name: accessibility_check
tools.description: Run the Accessibility Checker's full check (32 rules in 7 categories: document, page_content, forms, alternate_text, tables, lists, headings). Each rule is passed, failed (with findings and pages), manual (needs a person) or skipped. Findings on locatable figures, annotations and form widgets include bbox_user_space in PDF coordinates. Colour contrast is off unless all is true; rules (ids such as tagged-pdf, figures-alt-text) or categories narrow the check; pages limit the page rules.

tools.name: accessibility_figures
tools.description: The tagged figures (Figure elements, through the role map) in document order: figure number, page, alternate text and where the figure is drawn (top-left-origin points).

tools.name: accessibility_fix
tools.description: Apply the checker's automatic fix for a rule: primary-language (value: the language, e.g. en-US), title (value: the title; default the current title or file name; also shows it in the title bar) or tab-order (every page tabs in structure order). Returns the rule's new status. Undoable.

tools.name: accessibility_move_tag
tools.description: Move a reachable indirect structure tag before or after a direct sibling in their parent's /K array, changing tagged reading order without changing page appearance. Use object and generation values from accessibility_tags. Rejects distinct parents, duplicate references and positions that are already current. Undoable.

tools.name: accessibility_report
tools.description: Run the full check and write the accessibility report (HTML) to path; returns the results too. Takes the same options as accessibility_check.

tools.name: accessibility_review_html
tools.description: Compare two open versions of a PDF and write a self-contained HTML summary of the same evidence as accessibility_review_record: document hashes, outcome counts, rule changes, and rules still requiring review. Does not change either PDF or claim accessibility compliance.

tools.name: accessibility_review_load
tools.description: Read a local review sidecar only when its recorded SHA-256 matches the open PDF. Returns the decisions without changing the PDF.

tools.name: accessibility_review_record
tools.description: Compare the same accessibility rules on two open versions of a PDF and write a JSON record to path. Includes document SHA-256 hashes, before/after rule statuses and finding counts, changed rules, and rules still needing review. Does not change either PDF or claim accessibility compliance. Open the original and edited copies as separate documents.

tools.name: accessibility_review_save
tools.description: Write a local JSON sidecar for an open PDF with rule-level human review decisions. The sidecar records the PDF SHA-256; replacing one tied to different bytes requires replace: true. Does not change the PDF or assert compliance.

tools.name: accessibility_set_alt
tools.description: Set a figure's alternate text (alt; empty or omitted clears it), or mark it decorative (decorative: true: its content becomes an artifact and the figure leaves the tags). figure is a number from accessibility_figures. Returns the figures. Undoable.

tools.name: accessibility_set_tag_property
tools.description: Set or clear one property of a reachable indirect structure tag. Use object and generation from accessibility_tags. Properties: type, title, actual_text, alternate_text, language. Empty or omitted value clears text properties; type requires a nonempty PDF name. Undoable.

tools.name: accessibility_tags
tools.description: List reachable indirect structure tags in document order with PDF object number, generation, nearest indirect parent, depth, page, type, title, actual text, alternate text and language. Inline tag dictionaries have no stable object reference and are not listed.

tools.name: action_list
tools.description: Action Wizard: the built-in actions (name, description, steps) and every step an action can use (id, label, whether it takes a text argument).

tools.name: action_run
tools.description: Action Wizard: run a built-in action (action: its name) or a list of steps ([{step, arg}], ids from action_list) on each PDF in paths, writing the results into folder under the same names. Returns each file's step log or error.

tools.name: bookmark_add
tools.description: Add a bookmark that goes to a page, under a parent bookmark (or at the top level), at a position. Undoable.

tools.name: bookmark_delete
tools.description: Delete a bookmark and the bookmarks under it. Undoable.

tools.name: bookmark_from_structure
tools.description: Make bookmarks from the document's tagged headings (H, H1-H6), nested by level under a new first bookmark titled "Untitled". Fails if the document has no tagged headings. Returns the first page of the bookmark tree (see bookmark_list). Undoable.

tools.name: bookmark_list
tools.description: The bookmarks in outline order, one page at a time: each with its path (1-based, as the other bookmark tools take it), title, target page and open state, and its children on the same page. next is the offset of the following page, or null at the end. Bookmarks nested deeper than 33 levels are not listed.

tools.name: bookmark_move
tools.description: Move a bookmark (with its children) under another parent, or within its level. Undoable.

tools.name: bookmark_rename
tools.description: Change a bookmark's title. Undoable.

tools.name: bookmark_set_page
tools.description: Point a bookmark at another page. Undoable.

tools.name: command_batch
tools.description: Run steps in order (at most 1000). Returns completed/failed counts and per-step ok/result/error; stop_on_error defaults to true.

tools.name: command_list
tools.description: Every registered PdfCraft command with its menu, shortcut, whether it is enabled now, and the tool that automates it.

tools.name: command_run
tools.description: Run a registry command through its headless tool. Pass that tool's arguments in params (see command_list). Unknown params are ignored with warnings; path confinement still applies.

tools.name: comment_add
tools.description: Add a comment as Acrobat's commenting tools do. Geometry is in points with the origin at the top-left of the displayed page, y down (as in page_render images at 72 dpi and text_find rects). note: `at` [x, y] (icon top-left). stamp: `at` [x, y] (its centre) and `stamp`: approved, completed, confidential, draft, final, for comment, for public release, information only, not approved, not for public release, preliminary results, void, accepted, initial here, rejected, sign here, witness; dynamic: true for the dynamic approved/confidential/received/reviewed/revised stamps with a By … at … line. highlight/underline/strikeout/squiggly: `find` (text on the page to mark; every match with all: true) or `quads`. rectangle/oval/textbox: `rect` [x0, y0, x1, y1]. line/arrow: `from`, `to`. Optional `endings` (two names: start, end) for a line, arrow or polyline, or one name for a callout: None, Square, Circle, Diamond, OpenArrow, ClosedArrow, Butt, ROpenArrow, RClosedArrow, Slash. An arrow without endings is None then OpenArrow. ink: `strokes` [[[x, y], …], …]. polygon/cloud/polyline (connected lines): `points` [[x, y], …]. callout: `rect` (its text box), `to` (the point the arrow touches), optional `knee`. caret (inserted text): `at`, the insertion point on the baseline. replace (Replace Text): `find` or `quads` like highlight, `contents` the replacement. attachment: `path` (the file), `at`, optional `icon` (PushPin, Paperclip, Graph, Tag). Undoable. Text a text box, callout or stamp draws in the standard fonts that they can't draw (Chinese, Greek) is saved as typed and drawn as `?`; `warnings` in the result says so.

tools.name: comment_delete
tools.description: Delete a comment with its pop-up and replies. Undoable.

tools.name: comment_edit
tools.description: Change a comment's text, colour, opacity, line width, fill (rectangle/oval/polygon; "none" removes it), rectangle (rectangle/oval/text box/stamp) or position (`move` [dx, dy] in points). Stamps keep their original appearance when resized. One undo step.

tools.name: comment_image_preview
tools.description: Return a PNG of the page without the selected image signature/initials (layer=background, default), or its embedded image with alpha (layer=image). Includes the displayed rectangle, document rotation, image_rotation (how far clockwise the image is shown turned) and annotation opacity. Cache these layers for live placement/resizing; commit once with comment_edit. Does not change the document or undo history.

tools.name: comment_list
tools.description: Every comment (annotation other than links, form widgets and pop-ups) with its page, index, id, type, author, text, date, rectangle, colour, review status and replies.

tools.name: comment_lock
tools.description: Lock or unlock a comment (Properties ▸ Locked). Locked comments can't be moved, resized, restyled or deleted; their text stays editable. Undoable.

tools.name: comment_mark
tools.description: Mark or unmark a comment with a checkmark (Acrobat: Mark with checkmark), recorded as a private reply. Undoable.

tools.name: comment_reply
tools.description: Add a reply to a comment's thread. Undoable.

tools.name: comment_set_status
tools.description: Set a comment's review status (Acrobat: Set status), recorded as a status reply. Undoable.

tools.name: comments_hide
tools.description: Hide or show every comment on the page (fields and links still draw). A view setting: the file doesn't change.

tools.name: comments_summarize
tools.description: Make a PDF summarising every comment (number, author, type, date, text, replies), sorted by page, author, date or type.

tools.name: content_delete
tools.description: Delete an added item (page, index from content_list). Undoable.

tools.name: content_list
tools.description: Text and images added with page_add_text/page_add_image (or Edit a PDF ▸ Add content), per page with a 1-based index, rect (points from the top-left of the page), and text style.

tools.name: content_update
tools.description: Move/resize (rect), retype (text) or restyle (font, size, bold, italic, color, align) an added item (page, index from content_list). Images: rotate (degrees, multiple of 90, counter-clockwise), flip_h / flip_v (toggle), crop [left, bottom, right, top] as fractions trimmed, image (a file that replaces the picture). Undoable.

tools.name: doc_audit_redactions
tools.description: Find faux redactions: opaque filled rectangles painted over text that is still extractable, and /Redact annotations that were marked but never applied. Paint-order and colour-aware: a rectangle counts only when painted after the text and dark enough to hide it (page backgrounds and light shading are not flagged). Each finding reports the 1-based page, the kind (covered-text or unapplied-mark), the rectangle, and the hidden text. Fails closed: unreadable content is an error, never a clean bill. A properly applied redaction removes the text and never flags.

tools.name: doc_audit_space
tools.description: How many bytes each kind of content takes and its share of the file (PDF Optimizer ▸ Audit space usage): images, content streams, fonts, forms, comments, structure, bookmarks, … and document overhead.

tools.name: doc_background
tools.description: Fill page backgrounds with a colour, or a picture from `file` (an image, or page `file_page` of a PDF) fitted at `scale` (default 1), behind the content. Undoable.

tools.name: doc_batch
tools.description: Run convert, ocr and/or optimize over files and folders, one file at a time. recursive defaults to false. Preserve paths relative to each selected folder inside out_dir; duplicate inputs run once. Skip unsupported files, links and the output subtree. Existing outputs receive numbered names and are never replaced. Continue after per-file errors unless stop_on_error is true. Return completed/failed/skipped counts and per-file results. Discovery is bounded to 10000 entries and 64 folder levels. Convert must be first; each step can appear once. OCR uses installed models. Optimize uses Reduce File Size settings, optionally overriding target ppi (threshold 1.5 times ppi) and JPEG quality; a larger candidate keeps the original bytes. Sources and open documents are unchanged.

tools.name: doc_close
tools.description: Close a document. Fails if it has unsaved changes unless discard_changes is true.

tools.name: doc_combine
tools.description: Combine files, in order, into one PDF (bookmarks are kept under one entry per file). Images (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, GIF, BMP, JPEG 2000) and .txt files are made into PDFs first. pages optionally chooses each file's pages, in step with paths: a range such as "1-3, 6" or null for all pages. passwords, also in step with paths, opens encrypted files (the open password, or the permissions password where a file's security doesn't allow copying pages; null for none). The result is not encrypted. Passwords are never echoed back. groups, also in step with paths, splits a file around others: entries with the same number (they must name the same path) are one file, copied once, so it keeps one bookmark at its first page, its links and its form fields; null for a file of its own. A group uses its first entry's password. When two files' forms name the same field, field_conflicts says what happens: "rename" (the default) keeps the fields separate by renaming the later one (Text1 becomes Text1-1) and the result lists renamed_fields as [[old, new], …] — scripts that refer to the old name are not rewritten; "merge" makes them one field, as before.

tools.name: doc_compare
tools.description: Compare the text of two open documents: other is the older version, doc the newer. Returns counts and each change (replaced, inserted, deleted) with the old and new text, pages (1-based) and rectangles (points, origin bottom-left).

tools.name: doc_compare_mark
tools.description: Add the differences from other (older) to doc (newer) as comments in doc: highlights over replaced (blue) and inserted (green) text, notes where text was deleted (red), authored Compare. Undoable.

tools.name: doc_compare_report
tools.description: Write the compare summary report (a PDF listing every change) to path.

tools.name: doc_create
tools.description: Create a new, unsaved document and return it like doc_open: `blank` (pages, width, height in points; default 1 US Letter page), `images` (paths of PNG, JPEG, TIFF (every page), GIF or BMP files, one page each at the image's resolution) or `text` (a .txt path, or `text` directly; Western European (WinAnsi) characters only, others are refused). Save it with doc_save and a path.

tools.name: doc_create_multiple
tools.description: Convert several files (PDFs, PNG/JPEG/JPEG 2000/TIFF/GIF/BMP images, .txt files) to PDF in one run. mode "combine" (default) joins them, in order, into one PDF with a bookmark per file; pages optionally chooses each file's pages, in step with paths (a range such as "1-3, 6" or null). mode "separate" writes one PDF per file into out_dir (files that are already PDFs are skipped; existing files are never overwritten) and reports each file's result.

tools.name: doc_export_all_images
tools.description: Write the images that pages use into a folder (`<name>_Page_<n>_Image_<k>.jpg|png`), each once: JPEG images unchanged, others as PNG with their soft mask as alpha. min_size skips images with fewer pixels on their shorter side. Images that can't be decoded yet (JPEG 2000, JBIG2, CCITT, separations) are listed under skipped. Includes unsaved edits.

tools.name: doc_export_data
tools.description: Write comments and/or form data to path; the extension picks the format: .xfdf or .fdf (comments and/or fields), .xml, .csv or .txt (form data). For an XFA form, .xml is its data alone (rooted at the form's root data node, as Acrobat exports it) and .xdp an XML Data Package holding the whole datasets. what: all (default), comments, fields.

tools.name: doc_export_images
tools.description: Write pages as PNG, JPEG or TIFF files (`<name>_page_<n>.png|jpg|tif`) into a folder, at a resolution (default 150 dpi). JPEG and TIFF are flattened onto white paper. A page too large for the renderer at that resolution is drawn at the most it allows, listed in `lower_dpi` ({page, dpi}). Includes unsaved edits.

tools.name: doc_export_office
tools.description: Export a PDF ▸ Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx, one slide per page), HTML (.html, one file with images inline) or RTF (.rtf), chosen by path's extension: text, headings, bold and italic. Word uses borderless inferred tables and positioned editable shapes on pages with artwork, rotated or large text; each source page retains its size. Font matching and vector graphics remain limited.

tools.name: doc_export_text
tools.description: Write the reading-order text of pages to a .txt file (pages separated by form feeds).

tools.name: doc_flatten
tools.description: Merge comment and/or form field appearances into the page content, so they print and display everywhere but can no longer be edited. Undoable until saved.

tools.name: doc_header_footer
tools.description: Add a header and/or footer to pages. Text boxes: header_left/center/right, footer_left/center/right. Tokens: <<1>> page number, <<n>> page count, <<1 of n>>, <<Page 1 of n>>, <<1/n>>, dates <<m/d/yyyy>> <<yyyy-mm-dd>> <<mmmm d, yyyy>> (and more), Bates <<Bates Number#6#1#PREFIX#SUFFIX>>. replace: true swaps out existing ones (Update). Undoable.

tools.name: doc_hidden_info
tools.description: What Remove Hidden Information would remove, by category (metadata, attachments, comments, form-fields, hidden-text, hidden-layers, bookmarks, links-actions-scripts, private-data) with counts.

tools.name: doc_import_data
tools.description: Import comments and/or field values from an XFDF, FDF, XML, CSV or tab-delimited text file (detected from its content). Comments with the same name are replaced; values go through the form's formats and validation. For an XFA form, an XDP, datasets or data XML file replaces the form's data: a laid-out form is laid out again from it (rows included) and its calculations run. Undoable.

tools.name: doc_info
tools.description: Metadata, page sizes and labels, bookmarks, annotations, form fields, links, layers, attachments, fonts, security and repair notes.

tools.name: doc_initial_view
tools.description: Read or change how the document opens (Document Properties ▸ Initial View) and its reading options: navigation (page, bookmarks, pages, attachments, layers), layout (default, single, continuous, two_up, two_up_continuous, two_up_cover, two_up_continuous_cover), magnification (default, actual, fit_page, fit_width, fit_height, fit_visible, or a percentage), page, window options (fit_window, center_window, full_screen, display_title), interface options (hide_menubar, hide_toolbar, hide_window_ui), language and binding (left, right). Only the given ones change; returns the result. Undoable.

tools.name: doc_inspect
tools.description: With doc, return doc_info; otherwise return information for every open document (empty documents array when none are open).

tools.name: doc_list
tools.description: List the open documents with their ids, page counts and unsaved state.

tools.name: doc_open
tools.description: Open a PDF file and return its document id, page count and whether it can be edited.

tools.name: doc_open_revision
tools.description: Open saved revision `revision` (1 = the oldest) of a document as a new, unsaved document, to see the file as it was then.

tools.name: doc_optimize
tools.description: Write an optimized copy to `path` (Acrobat's PDF Optimizer). color / gray: { downsample, ppi, above_ppi, compression: jpeg|zip|retain, quality 1–100 } (defaults: downsample to 150 ppi above 225, JPEG 60). Images are measured where pages draw them and replaced only when smaller. discard_*: thumbnails (default true), alternate_images (true), tags, print_settings; flate_unencoded (true); remove_invalid_links and remove_unreferenced_dests (true); images and forms the pages list but never draw are always dropped (unused_xobjects). discard: Remove Hidden Information categories (metadata, attachments, comments, form-fields, hidden-text, hidden-layers, bookmarks, links-actions-scripts, private-data). Signed documents are refused. The open document is unchanged.

tools.name: doc_print
tools.description: Print with Acrobat's Print dialog options, or save the print-ready PDF. pages: a range such as "1-3, 6, 9-" (page labels allowed; default all); subset odd/even; reverse. layout: fit (default), actual, shrink, custom (scale %), multiple (per_sheet 2/4/6/9/16, order, border, auto_rotate; cut-stack order arranges single-sided sheets for cutting into piles and stacking left to right, top to bottom, keeping sheet order within each pile; duplex must be off), booklet (booklet_subset both/front/back, binding left/right), poster (scale %, overlap pt, cut_marks). orientation auto/portrait/landscape; comments_forms document / document-and-markups (default) / document-and-stamps / form-fields-only; paper Letter/Legal/Tabloid, ARCH A/B/C/D/E1/E, ANSI C/D/E, or A0/A1/A2/A3/A4/A5 (short names or full preset labels); use layout actual for 100% in the print-ready PDF; printer drivers may still substitute paper or scale. Then path (save) or printer (a name or "default") with copies, collate, duplex off/long-edge/short-edge, grayscale, and options (driver options from printer_options, CUPS).

tools.name: doc_protect
tools.description: Encrypt the document (applied by the next doc_save, a full rewrite). open_password is needed to open it. permissions_password is needed to change security and lifts the restrictions given by printing/changes/copy/accessibility; those restrictions (and their defaults) apply only when permissions_password is given. With open_password alone the document is encrypted and everything stays allowed, so passing a restriction without permissions_password is an error. Passwords are never echoed back. Undoable.

tools.name: doc_reduce
tools.description: Write a smaller copy of the document to `path` with Acrobat's Reduce File Size choices: images above 225 ppi downsampled to 150 ppi and JPEG-compressed (medium quality), thumbnails dropped, identical fonts and images merged, unused objects dropped, compressed object streams. If the copy wouldn't be smaller, nothing is written and `written` is false. The open document is unchanged.

tools.name: doc_remove_hidden
tools.description: Remove the listed categories (see doc_hidden_info), or every category when none are listed (Sanitize Document). Form fields are flattened so their values stay visible. The next save rewrites the whole file. Undoable until saved.

tools.name: doc_remove_marks
tools.description: Remove every header and footer, watermark or background PdfCraft (or a compatible tool) added. Undoable.

tools.name: doc_revisions
tools.description: List the document's saved revisions (oldest first): each incremental update is one. Returns revision number, where it ends in the file and its size, and which signatures sign exactly that revision.

tools.name: doc_save
tools.description: Save to its own file (an incremental update, which keeps signatures valid) or to a new path (a full rewrite). The write is atomic. flatten_fill_sign bakes Fill & Sign text, marks and signatures into the page first and removes those annotations; other comments and form fields stay. Omit it, or pass false, to leave them editable.

tools.name: doc_set_info
tools.description: Set a document information entry such as Title, Author, Subject or Keywords; an empty value removes it. When the file has XMP metadata, the matching XMP property (dc:title, dc:creator, dc:description, pdf:Keywords, xmp:CreatorTool, pdf:Producer) is changed too, so viewers that read XMP first show the new value. Undoable.

tools.name: doc_split
tools.description: Split into several files written to out_dir: every N pages, before given pages, at top-level bookmarks (bookmarks: true; files named after them, repeated titles get -2, -3), or by file size (max_mb). Files are <name>-partK.pdf.

tools.name: doc_unprotect
tools.description: Remove password security (the document must have been opened with its permissions password, or have none). Applied by the next doc_save. Undoable.

tools.name: doc_watermark
tools.description: Add a watermark to pages: text, or a picture from `file` (an image, or page `file_page` of a PDF) at `scale` of the page (default 0.5); rotated (degrees counter-clockwise, default 45), semi-transparent (opacity 0–1, default 0.5), text fitted to the page unless font_size is given, on top unless behind: true; moved from the page centre by `offset_x` (right) and `offset_y` (up) points (default 0). replace: true swaps out existing ones. Undoable.

tools.name: edit_redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone edit of a document.

tools.name: edit_undo
tools.description: Undo the last edit of a document.

tools.name: fill_sign_add
tools.description: Fill in a form that has no fields, as Acrobat's Fill & Sign does: type text (`text`, default 10 pt; `font_size` 4–300 pt), place a check, cross, dot or line, today's date (in Preferences ▸ Date format, see fill_sign_date_format, or `format`; `font_size` also applies), or a signature or initials (either `text` drawn in a script font, or `path` to a local PNG/JPEG image up to 4 MiB and 32 megapixels, scaled down to 4 megapixels, preserving transparency; with `scan: true`, `path` is instead a photo of a signature on paper, within the same limits: the signature is found, and the paper, shadows and table around it are removed, with `sensitivity` 0–100, default 50, picking up fainter ink when higher). `at` [x, y] is in points from the top-left of the page: text's top-left, mark's centre, signature's left edge centred vertically. Image signatures fit within 150 pt wide and 32 pt tall (24 pt for initials). Creates movable, undoable annotations. Typed text the standard fonts can't draw is saved and drawn as `?` (`warnings` in the result says so); a typed signature neither the script font nor its fallback can draw is refused (pass `path` instead).

tools.name: fill_sign_date_format
tools.description: Preferences ▸ Date format: the pattern Fill & Sign dates use (default m/d/yyyy). Set it with `format` (Acrobat date codes yyyy yy mmmm mmm mm m dddd ddd dd d, other runs of y, m or d are refused; H h M s t are time letters and need \ before them; \ shows the next character as is), or read it. `language` sets the language of month and weekday names (a code from `languages`, or `auto` to follow the app's interface language; English headless). Returns the format, the language, today in them, `unwritable` (characters of today's date that Fill & Sign can't write into a PDF yet, Western European only; fill_sign_add refuses such a date), the ready-made presets and the languages.

tools.name: form_actions
tools.description: Field Properties ▸ Actions: the field's action for each trigger (mouse_up, mouse_down, mouse_enter, mouse_exit, on_focus, on_blur).

tools.name: form_add_field
tools.description: Add a form field on a page. type: text, date, checkbox, radio, combo, list, button, image (a picture placeholder; fill it with form_set_image), signature. rect in points from the top-left of the displayed page [x0, y0, x1, y1]. name defaults to Acrobat's next free name (Text1, Check Box1, Group1, Dropdown1, List Box1, Button1, Image1, Signature1, Date1). Radio buttons join the radio group named by group (a new group otherwise) with the export value export. Returns the field's name. Undoable.

tools.name: form_delete_field
tools.description: Delete a form field and all its widgets. Undoable.

tools.name: form_detect_fields
tools.description: Prepare a form ▸ automatic field detection: find the blanks a printed form asks to be filled (underscore runs, lines, empty boxes, small squares for check boxes) and name each field from its label. With add (default true) the fields are created as one undoable step; otherwise they are only proposed. Returns page (1-based), kind, name and rect (points, origin bottom-left).

tools.name: form_fields
tools.description: Every interactive form field: name, type (text, checkbox, radio, combo, list, button, signature), value, options, page, rect (top-left-origin points) and rotation (0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees counterclockwise), read-only and required flags.

tools.name: form_fill
tools.description: Set several fields at once (one undo step). values maps field names (from form_fields) to: a string for text fields, combo boxes and radio groups (an option), true/false for check boxes, an array of strings for multi-select lists. Appearances are regenerated so every viewer shows the values. A value whose characters the field's font can't draw (Chinese in a Helvetica field) is still saved; `warnings` in the result names the field and character: PdfCraft draws `?` there and asks other viewers to redraw the field from its value.

tools.name: form_merge_data
tools.description: Collect the field values of form data files (FDF, XFDF) or filled-in PDF forms into one CSV file at path: a column per field name, a row per file. Returns the row and column counts.

tools.name: form_reset
tools.description: Reset fields to their default values: all of them, or only those listed. Undoable.

tools.name: form_set_actions
tools.description: Field Properties ▸ Actions: replace the field's actions. Each item: trigger (mouse_up, mouse_down, mouse_enter, mouse_exit, on_focus, on_blur) and one of javascript (source), url, reset (field names; [] for all), menu (Print, NextPage, PrevPage, FirstPage, LastPage), page (1-based), show / hide (field names), submit (URL). Triggers not listed lose their action. Undoable.

tools.name: form_set_image
tools.description: Show an image file (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, GIF or BMP) in an image field or button, scaled to fit and centred (what clicking an image field does). On an XFA form the picture is kept in its data too (base64, as Designer saves it) and the form shows it from there. Undoable.

tools.name: form_set_props
tools.description: Change field properties: give field for one field, or fields for a list of unique field names (1–1000). A bulk change is atomic and one Undo step; an invalid or locked field leaves every field unchanged. Only the given properties change, and partial appearance changes preserve each field's other colours and font. name (rename), rect (position) and rotation require a single field. General and Options: tooltip, read_only, required, multiline, max_length (0 = no limit), options (combo/list items), font_size (0 = auto), format, validate, calculate (Acrobat's native AF rules). Options: align (left, center, right), default (Reset form's value; check boxes/radio buttons use their on state, "" for off), flags { scroll, rich_text, password, file_select, spell_check, comb (needs max_length), sort, editable, multi_select, commit_immediately }, check_style (check boxes/radio buttons: check, circle, cross, diamond, square, star). rotation is 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees counterclockwise and swaps width/height when the axis changes. Undoable.

tools.name: form_set_script
tools.description: Field Properties ▸ Run custom script: set field's JavaScript for event keystroke, format, validate or calculate (the field's actions; calculated fields join the calculation order) or mouse_up (a button's action). Omit script to remove it. The scripts use Acrobat's object model (event.value, event.rc, getField, util.printf, …) and run when the field changes. Undoable.

tools.name: form_tab_order
tools.description: Set the tab order of pages (default all): row (top to bottom, left to right), column, structure, or annotations (unspecified). Or order tabs manually: `field` with `move` earlier|later moves that field one place on its page. Returns the resulting order of fields. Undoable.

tools.name: image_edit
tools.description: Change one of a page's images (number from page_images): action move (rect: new full placement box in top-left-origin points, based on page_images.rect), rotate (quarters clockwise, default 1), flip_horizontal, flip_vertical, replace (path: an image file, drawn in the same place) or delete. Undoable. The selected image crop transforms with its pixels, isolating shared path scopes while retaining neighboring painting. Text-outline clips return a clear error. Rotation/flip use the visible centre. Form artwork supports move/resize/rotate/flip/delete as a group; replace and image_save only support raster images.

tools.name: image_hit
tools.description: List image/Form numbers whose placement and all clipping paths contain point [x,y] in top-left-origin points. Bezier curves, even-odd/nonzero fill and holes are respected. Read only.

tools.name: image_save
tools.description: Write one of a page's raster images (number from page_images; forms are refused) to path: JPEG images unchanged, others as PNG (the extension is added when missing).

tools.name: js_document_scripts
tools.description: List the document-level JavaScripts (name and source), which define functions field scripts use.

tools.name: js_enabled
tools.description: Preferences ▸ JavaScript ▸ Enable Acrobat JavaScript: set it with `enabled`, or read it. With JavaScript off, field scripts other than Acrobat's AF calls don't run.

tools.name: js_run
tools.description: Run Acrobat JavaScript in the document, as the JavaScript console does (or as push button `field`'s Mouse Up script when field is given; on a laid-out XFA form, `field` runs that button's XFA click script instead, JavaScript or FormCalc, which can add and remove rows and show or hide subforms). The form object model is available: this/getField, event, app, util, console, display, color, and the document-level scripts. Field changes and resetForm are applied as one undoable step; returns the script's alerts, console output, requests (print, page, url, submit) and error.

tools.name: js_set_document_script
tools.description: Add or replace the document-level JavaScript `name` with `script`, or delete it (script omitted). Undoable.

tools.name: link_add
tools.description: Add a link over rect on page that opens url or goes to to_page. Appearance: visible (rectangle), color, width 1-3, highlight none/invert/outline/inset. Undoable.

tools.name: link_delete
tools.description: Delete one link (page, index from link_list). Undoable.

tools.name: link_edit
tools.description: Change a link's rect, destination (url or to_page) or appearance. Undoable.

tools.name: link_list
tools.description: Every link: page, 1-based index (for link_edit/link_delete), rect (points from the top-left of the page), and where it goes (url or to_page).

tools.name: link_open
tools.description: Follow a local GoToR link in PdfCraft: open the referenced PDF as a new document, respecting --root. page and index use link_list numbering. Named destinations are reported but not applied. Absolute file specifications require allow_absolute: true after reviewing the target; relative links need no opt-in.

tools.name: links_from_urls
tools.description: Find web addresses (http://, https://, www.) in the text of every page and make them clickable links. Returns the URLs. Undoable.

tools.name: links_remove
tools.description: Remove every link in the document (or on the given pages). Undoable.

tools.name: measure_area
tools.description: Add an undoable area annotation from a simple polygon. The last edge closes automatically.

tools.name: measure_distance
tools.description: Add an undoable two-point distance annotation using the scale of the first point's viewport.

tools.name: measure_export
tools.description: Atomically write saved measurement values, labels, authors and scale ratios as spreadsheet-safe CSV. Returns how many unsupported measurements were left out.

tools.name: measure_info
tools.description: Calculate a live distance, perimeter or area, deltas, angle and scale without adding an annotation. Incomplete paths are allowed.

tools.name: measure_list
tools.description: Saved measurement annotations with calculated values, scale and vertices in display coordinates. Measurements with unsupported imported formats (compound or fractional units, non-rectilinear scales) or invalid geometry are listed under unsupported with a reason.

tools.name: measure_perimeter
tools.description: Add an undoable connected-line length annotation. To include a closing edge, repeat the first point at the end.

tools.name: measure_scale
tools.description: Read the scale at a point, or add a rectangular viewport using units_per_point or two calibration points and their real-world distance. Existing measurements retain their original scales. Undoable.

tools.name: measure_snap
tools.description: Snap a point to vector paths, endpoints, midpoints or intersections. Coordinates and tolerance are in display points. Bounded extraction reports truncated geometry.

tools.name: object_list
tools.description: List existing paragraphs, Image/Form artwork and added content once, with source kind/index references, displayed rectangles and document generation. Indexes change when content changes; use generation in object_move to reject stale references.

tools.name: object_move
tools.description: Atomically translate 1–1000 mixed references from object_list by [dx, dy] in displayed points (right/down). Preserves glyph codes, fonts, image data and relative spacing; success is one undo step. Clipping and vertical text are refused. A bad/stale reference refuses the entire move.

tools.name: ocr_recognize
tools.description: Scan & OCR ▸ Recognize text: render pages, read the words in them and add them as invisible text over the page image, so scanned pages become searchable and selectable (a searchable image; the image is not changed). Pages that already have text are skipped unless skip_text_pages is false; then pictures on those pages are read too, and recognised words that the page's own text already has (an earlier OCR layer included) are left out and counted as already_on_page. Returns each page's recognised text, word count or why it was skipped. Needs the OCR models (ocr_status). Undoable as one step.

tools.name: ocr_recognize_files
tools.description: Scan & OCR ▸ Recognize text ▸ In multiple files: read every page of each PDF in paths and write the searchable result into folder under the same name (pages that already have text are left alone unless skip_text_pages is false, as in ocr_recognize). Returns, per file, the output path, word count and skipped pages, or the error.

tools.name: ocr_status
tools.description: Whether text recognition is available (its models are installed: release packages include them; a source build fetches them with `cargo xtask models`; PDFCRAFT_MODELS overrides), where it looks for them, and the languages it reads.

tools.name: page_add_image
tools.description: Add an image file (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, GIF, BMP) as page content: in rect (points from the top-left of the page), or centred at its natural size (shrunk to fit). Undoable; movable with content_update.

tools.name: page_add_text
tools.description: Add text as page content (not a comment). Place it with at [x, y] (top-left, points from the top-left of the displayed page) and width (wrap width, default 200), or rect. Newlines start new lines; long lines wrap. Style: font helvetica/times/courier, size, bold, italic, color (#RRGGBB or a name), align left/center/right. Text must be Western European (WinAnsi) characters; others are refused. It stays editable with content_update. Undoable.

tools.name: page_delete
tools.description: Delete pages. Undoable until saved.

tools.name: page_duplicate
tools.description: Insert copies of pages after the last of them (fonts and images are shared, not copied). Undoable.

tools.name: page_enhance_camera
tools.description: Straighten a photographed document (Scan & OCR ▸ Enhance ▸ Camera image): the part of the page inside the four corners (x1, y1, … x4, y4 in top-left-origin points, any order, a convex quadrilateral; when omitted, the document's edges are found automatically, or an error says they could not be) is warped to an upright rectangle that replaces what the page shows, at the page picture's own resolution (at most 600 dpi). mode is how it looks: original, colour (default), greyscale or bw (black and white, stored losslessly). level (0–100, default 0) then cleans the photo up: even lighting so the paper turns white (casts, shadows, dark edges), more contrast, and from 60 no isolated specks; colour ink stays colour. For bw the level is the threshold (higher keeps fainter strokes black). The page's comments, links and bookmarks stay. Undoable.

tools.name: page_extract
tools.description: Copy pages into a new PDF (links, bookmarks, fields and layers that belong to them come along). separate: true writes each page as its own file into out_dir; delete: true removes the pages from this document afterwards (undoable).

tools.name: page_images
tools.description: The raster images and grouped Form artwork a page draws (Edit a PDF): number, full placement rect and visible_rect after page/path clipping (top-left-origin points; null if fully hidden), kind (image/form), pixel size ([0,0] for forms) and resource name. Forms include nested graphics and are edited as a whole. Numbers count forms and images together in drawing order, so a page with forms numbers its images differently than before forms were listed: always take numbers from a fresh page_images call.

tools.name: page_insert_blank
tools.description: Insert a blank page so it becomes page `at`. Size defaults to the neighbouring page. Undoable.

tools.name: page_insert_file
tools.description: Insert pages of another PDF so the first becomes page `at`. Undoable.

tools.name: page_move
tools.description: Move pages so the first of them lands at position `to` (1-based, counted before the move). Undoable.

tools.name: page_number
tools.description: Label a range of pages (e.g. i, ii, iii for front matter, or A-1, A-2 for an appendix). Later pages keep their labels. Undoable.

tools.name: page_render
tools.description: Render one page to a PNG image (default 96 dpi, at most 600).

tools.name: page_replace
tools.description: Replace the content of pages with pages of another PDF (same count). Links, comments, form fields and bookmarks on the original pages stay, as in Acrobat. Undoable.

tools.name: page_rotate
tools.description: Rotate pages by a multiple of 90 degrees (positive is clockwise): the listed pages (default all), filtered like Acrobat's Rotate Pages by subset (all, even, odd page numbers) and orientation (all, landscape, portrait). Undoable.

tools.name: page_set_box
tools.description: Set a page box (crop by default; also trim, bleed, art, media) on pages: either margins in points from the media box [left, bottom, right, top], or an absolute rect in points from the top-left of the displayed page. Omit both to reset the box to its default. Undoable.

tools.name: pdfa_convert
tools.description: Standards ▸ Save as PDF/A: fix what can be fixed for PDF/A-2b or 3b (XMP identification and metadata, an sRGB output intent, forbidden actions and JavaScript, annotation print flags, image interpolation, encryption). Returns what was fixed and what remains (e.g. fonts that aren't embedded). Undoable; save the document to keep it.

tools.name: pdfa_verify
tools.description: Standards ▸ Verify PDF/A compliance: the PDF/A-2b or 3b rules the document breaks (ISO 19005 clause, message, page, whether Save as PDF/A can fix it), plus what it declares.

tools.name: print_readiness
tools.description: Verification only. Reports effective image resolution where each image is drawn (not against the page size), page boxes and bleed past the trim, output intents, fonts that are not embedded, and the PDF/A-2b structural result. Does not modify the document, embed fonts, invent a press profile, or check PDF/X.

tools.name: printer_options
tools.description: A printer driver's own job options (CUPS: from its PPD), such as the paper tray, paper type or finishing: key, label, group, default and choices. Pass chosen values to doc_print as options. Empty on Windows, where the driver's preferences window holds them.

tools.name: printers
tools.description: The printers the system's print spooler knows (CUPS on macOS and Linux), with the default marked.

tools.name: redact_apply
tools.description: Apply the redaction marks (all, or those on pages): text, images, vectors, comments and form fields under them are removed for good and boxes are drawn in their place. A verification pass fails the operation if anything readable remains. Undoable until saved; the saved file no longer contains the content.

tools.name: redact_clear
tools.description: Remove every redaction mark without applying it. Undoable.

tools.name: redact_mark
tools.description: Mark content for redaction (nothing is removed until redact_apply). One of: rect [x0, y0, x1, y1] (points from the top-left of the displayed page) with page; find (text, every match); words (a list of words or phrases, every match of each; the result's matched_words says how many marks each made); pattern (phone, email, credit-card, ssn, date: every match, Acrobat's Search & Redact patterns); whole_pages: true. find and words accept case_sensitive and whole_words (both default false). find, words, pattern and whole_pages work on pages (default all). overlay: text shown on the box once applied, or code_set (foia: U.S. FOIA (b)(1)(A)…(b)(9); privacy-act: U.S. Privacy Act (d)(5), (j)(1)…(k)(7)) with codes, shown as "(b)(6), (b)(7)(C)"; fill: box colour (default black). Undoable.

tools.name: render_preview
tools.description: Render a PNG bounded by max_side (default 1024), without changing or saving the document. Page defaults to 1; doc may be omitted when exactly one document is open.

tools.name: sign_document
tools.description: Sign with a digital ID (a .p12/.pfx path, or on macOS a Keychain identity: "keychain:<common name or fingerprint>" from sign_keychain_ids, or on Windows a store identity: "windows:<common name or fingerprint>" from sign_windows_ids) and save the signed file to `out` (signing always saves, as in Acrobat; the document then shows the signed file). Sign an existing empty signature field (`field`), or a new one on `page` at `rect` (omit rect for an invisible signature). certify: no_changes, form_fill or comments makes a certification signature. graphic shows a picture where the signer's name would be large (Acrobat: Configure Signature Appearance): {"image": path} (PNG or JPEG), {"text": name} (typed in the Fill & Sign script font) or {"strokes": [[[x, y], …], …]} (y up, the drawing pad 1 wide); it needs a visible signature. PAdES B-B, SHA-256 (SHA-384 for P-384 keys).

tools.name: sign_id_create
tools.description: Create a self-signed digital ID and save it as a password-protected .p12 file (Acrobat: Configure a new digital ID ▸ Create a new digital ID ▸ Save to file). Default key: 2048-bit RSA, valid 5 years.

tools.name: sign_keychain_ids
tools.description: macOS: the signing identities in the user's keychains (certificate details and the keychain: reference sign_document takes). The private keys stay in the Keychain, which may ask the user to allow their use.

tools.name: sign_list
tools.description: Every signature field with its validation: status (valid, unknown = intact but the signer isn't trusted, invalid, unsigned), signer and certificate, date, reason, location, certification level, page and rect, the revision it covers and changes made after signing (none, allowed, disallowed), with Acrobat-style explanations.

tools.name: sign_trust
tools.description: Add certificates (.cer/.crt/.pem/.der, or the certificates in a .p12 with `password`) to the trusted certificates used to validate signatures, or clear the list (clear: true). Every open document is revalidated. Returns the trusted list.

tools.name: sign_windows_ids
tools.description: Windows: signing identities in the Current User Personal certificate store (certificate details and the windows: reference sign_document takes). Private keys remain in CNG; Windows may ask permission to use them. `unusable` lists the store's other certificates with why they can't sign (no private key, an unsupported key type, a key CNG can't open).

tools.name: stamp_custom
tools.description: Stamp a picture: a PDF page (file_page, default 1) or an image file, centred at at [x, y] (points from the top-left of the displayed page) at its natural size, at most 200 pt. name labels it (default: the file name). Undoable.

tools.name: text_edit
tools.description: Replace the text of one paragraph (paragraph, from text_paragraphs: rewrapped to the paragraph's width with its line spacing) or one line (line, from text_lines) in place, keeping position, size and colour. For a mixed-style region, editor_text supplies visual row breaks; surviving text keeps its source-run styles and inserted text inherits the surrounding run. For a paragraph, also change its formatting: font (helvetica, times, courier) with bold/italic, size (points), color (#rrggbb), align (left, center, right, justify), underline, line_spacing (× size), char_spacing (points) and scale (horizontal, percent), or move it (dx, dy in points; up is +dy) and rewrap it to a new width (points); text may then be omitted. Its own font is reused when it can show every character and no font/weight change is requested; otherwise it uses a standard font matching the source style or, for Japanese and other text no standard font can show (Cyrillic, Greek), real Mincho/Gothic fallback outlines matching the requested/source family and available weight, from a face that has every character (the result shows the font used). Missing Japanese weights use Regular, not synthetic bold; the small web build has only Gothic Regular. Paragraph bold may be set without font to keep the source family. Text that no available font can show is refused. Undoable.

tools.name: text_edit_layout
tools.description: Measure a paragraph draft using the same PDF rewrite as Apply, without changing the document. Returns source_rect, draft_rect (top-left-origin points), overflow, and the embedded sfnt source faces available to the inline editor. Text defaults to the unchanged paragraph. Optional size, width, font_resource and disjoint UTF-8 ranges preview formatting changes.

tools.name: text_extract
tools.description: Extract the text of some or all pages, in reading order. With rect, only the text inside that rectangle on each page, as Column select takes it: one row per visual line, side-by-side pieces (table cells) separated by a tab.

tools.name: text_find
tools.description: Find a phrase (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalised) and return matches in page order with page and line rectangles in points (origin top-left). Reads growing batches, looking one match past the limit for a continuation. Failed pages do not discard readable matches: warnings contains up to 100 {page, error, error_truncated} entries (errors capped at 1024 UTF-8 bytes), warning_count counts failed pages, and warnings_truncated reports a capped list. complete is false after a page failure or when more matches exist; next is present only for a match-limit continuation.

tools.name: text_font_files
tools.description: Discover openly licensed, embeddable TrueType/OpenType files on request. Optional directories (at most 16) restrict the scan; with --root, only that root is scanned by default and supplied folders must stay inside it. The scan skips symlinks, collections and invalid/licence-restricted fonts, with depth, entry and byte budgets. Select a returned path with text_font_import.

tools.name: text_font_import
tools.description: Load an explicitly selected, openly licensed full TrueType/OpenType face into a page. The program's family, embedding permissions and licence declaration are validated. Completes source subsets of the same face without replacing existing glyphs. Returns a font resource usable with text_edit.font_resource. Undoable; respects root confinement. No system-interface fallback is exported.

tools.name: text_fonts
tools.description: List validated embedded source faces and approved full preview faces for a page. Full registered resources can be selected by text_edit.font_resource; preview_only faces are not PDF resource names.

tools.name: text_lines
tools.description: The lines of existing text on a page (Edit a PDF ▸ Edit text): number, text, box (top-left-origin points), font and size. Use the number with text_edit.

tools.name: text_paragraphs
tools.description: The paragraphs on a page (adjacent source runs grouped into aligned visual rows, including mixed fonts, sizes and colours): number, text, editor_text (visual rows separated by newlines), rows and source line numbers, box (top-left-origin points), font and size. Use the number with text_edit's paragraph.

tools.name: view_reading_colors
tools.description: Set the document's reading colours (Acrobat's Replace Document Colors, in the Reading Options): solid text and line-art paints are remapped for readability and the page clears to the background colour in page_render. A view setting: the file doesn't change. mode is one of: off, black-on-white, white-on-black, yellow-on-black, green-on-black, or custom (which takes text and background as #RRGGBB). only_black maps only near-black paints (default false) and line_art also maps line-art paints (default true); both override the mode's preset. A flag that differs from the mode's preset default makes the returned mode read custom, because the resulting params no longer match any preset. Returns the resulting setting.
